title: The pawnshop Stradivarius and his father's violin
summary: Jones brings home a pawnshop violin labeled Stradivarius and his father, unexpectedly, picks it up and plays; he learned of his father's honors only at his funeral.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: But I came home with a violin out of a pawnshop one day, and I saw the name Stradivarius on it. But I didn't see the word imitation. And my father just looked at me and picked it up and started playing it.

I was going to junior college in Chicago. I guess I must have been about 17, maybe. 17 -- maybe about 17 years old. And I guess it was inevitable that I would probably end up with someone like Stuff Smith, because the
And that was the first time your father ever played violin in front of you?
What did it date back to? Did you ask him, when --

No, he just picked it up and said, "No, James." I had a -- oh, a little discussion with another student. He said, "Man, that's not a Stradivarius. It can't be." You know. So I was in my ego trip, and I said, "Yes, it is. It says so on here." So I took it home and my father told me the same thing. He said, "No, James, this is not a Stradivarius," and picked it up and started playing it. You know.
He didn't tell you whether -- where he had learned or when he had played it before?
No. I didn't know he was the honor student that he was until his service, his funeral, you know? He was just very -- he was a modest man. He just never said anything about it.
